title: The Cloth-Washer and the Boastful Trooper
summary: Beside the river Barada in Damascus lived an honest cloth-washer and his witty wife, who earned their living washing carpets and linens. One afternoon, a boastful cavalry troope...
keywords: tale of the fuller and his wife and the trooper
full_text:
Beside the river Barada in Damascus lived an honest cloth-washer and his witty wife, who earned their living washing carpets and linens. One afternoon, a boastful cavalry trooper rode his horse into their drying meadow, trampling their clean white linens and threatening to strike the fuller with his scabbard if he did not wash his muddy saddlecloth immediately without pay.

The fuller was intimidated by the soldier’s sword, but his wife stepped forward with a cheerful smile:

'Welcome, valiant warrior! A hero of your martial renown deserves to have his saddlecloth washed in our special imperial soap-vat, which preserves the leather forever. But our vat is deep; if you will hold this willow pole and stir the boiling suds, the honor will be completed in an instant!'

The vain trooper, flattered by her praise, dismounted, leaned over the stone soap-vat, and began to stir the foam.

Quick as lightning, the fuller’s wife gave the soldier’s heavy boots a sudden shove! The boastful trooper plunged headfirst into the warm soapy suds, spluttering, soaked in foam from head to toe, his iron helmet clattering like an empty pot!

The fuller seized the soldier’s horse by the bridle, while his wife called for the city watchmen.

When the magistrate arrived, he laughed heartily at the dripping 'hero' who had been conquered by a bucket of soap, fined the trooper twenty dinars for damaging the clean linens, and awarded the money to the fuller, teaching the arrogant soldier that bullying working folk brings slippery consequences.
moral: Quiet common sense and presence of mind can outsmart the most arrogant bully.
